baslik: Raw Honey vs Sugar: What It Does to Blood Sugar
yorum: Do you use honey or sugar in your tea or oatmeal? Has your doctor or diabetes educator ever told you how to count it?
aciklama_giris:
Is honey kinder to your blood sugar than table sugar? A 2022 analysis from the University of Toronto pooled 18 controlled trials and 1,105 people and found small average improvements: fasting glucose about 4 milligrams per deciliter lower. But most of the evidence was low certainty, the glucose effect faded after adjusting for publication bias, and the trials were mostly in younger, healthier people.

In this video we look at what honey is made of, how its glycemic index compares with sugar, what the Toronto analysis found for raw and single-flower honey, why those results are shakier than they look, how a tablespoon fits into American Heart Association added-sugar limits, and five practical ways to use honey.
kaynaklar: Ahmed A, Tul-Noor Z, Lee D, et al. Effect of honey on cardiometabolic risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nutrition Reviews. 2023;81(7):758-774 (online 2022). DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuac086. PMID 36379223.

Yaghoobi N, Al-Waili N, Ghayour-Mobarhan M, et al. Natural honey and cardiovascular risk factors; effects on blood glucose, cholesterol, triacylglycerole, CRP, and body weight compared with sucrose. ScientificWorldJournal. 2008;8:463-469. DOI 10.1100/tsw.2008.64. PMID 18454257.

Bahrami M, Ataie-Jafari A, Hosseini S, et al. Effects of natural honey consumption in diabetic patients: an 8-week randomized clinical trial. International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition. 2009;60(7):618-626. DOI 10.3109/09637480801990389.
Erejuwa OO. Effect of honey in diabetes mellitus: matters arising. Journal of Diabetes & Metabolic Disorders. 2014;13:23. PMID 24476150.
Atkinson FS, Foster-Powell K, Brand-Miller JC. International tables of glycemic index and glycemic load values: 2008. Diabetes Care. 2008;31(12):2281-2283. PMID 18835944.

Johnson RK, Appel LJ, Brands M, et al. Dietary sugars intake and cardiovascular health: a scientific statement from the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2009;120:1011-1020. DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.109.192627.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Final guidance on the declaration of added sugars on honey, maple syrup, and certain cranberry products. 2019.
Mayo Clinic. Diabetes foods: Can I substitute honey for sugar? Expert answers, Diabetes.

kapak.gorsel: a large jar of golden honey with a wooden honey dipper dripping honey, a small mound of white sugar in front and a glucose meter with a blank screen overlapping the jar, close up and very large

sahneler.metin: If you've switched to honey to be kind to your blood sugar, here's what 18 trials found: fasting glucose fell by about 4 milligrams per deciliter.
sahneler.gorsel: a glass jar of golden honey with a wooden honey dipper dripping into a teacup, a glucose meter with a blank screen beside the jar

sahneler.metin: But the drop was small, the evidence weak, and it depended on the honey.
sahneler.gorsel: a spoonful of honey held above a bowl of white table sugar, a jar of honey behind, a gentle scale tipping only slightly

sahneler.metin: By the end, you'll know whether honey earns a place in your kitchen, and how to count it.
sahneler.gorsel: a kitchen shelf with a jar of honey, a sugar bowl and a wooden spoon, soft morning light drawn as fine lines

sahneler.metin: This is The Food Almanac. Let's start with what's actually inside a spoonful of honey.
sahneler.gorsel: a close view of a wooden honey dipper lifting honey from a jar, a honeycomb beside it, a beehive sketch in the corner

sahneler.metin: Honey is mostly sugar. A typical honey is roughly 38 percent fructose, 31 percent glucose, and 17 percent water, with only about one percent sucrose.
sahneler.gorsel: an open jar of honey beside a honeycomb, small golden spheres and pale spheres rising from the honey in a tidy cluster

sahneler.metin: Table sugar is sucrose, a molecule that joins one glucose and one fructose together. Your gut splits it apart, so you absorb the same two sugars that honey already holds loose.
sahneler.gorsel: a bowl of white table sugar with a spoon, beside a jar of honey, a simple pair of hexagon rings joined together on one side and separated on the other

sahneler.metin: Honey also contains small amounts of other plant compounds, and some researchers suggest these may matter. Much of that work has been in rats, though. By weight, a jar of honey is mainly sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with clover flowers and a honeybee resting on the rim, a glass of tea nearby

sahneler.metin: One way to compare foods is the glycemic index, which ranks how fast a food raises blood sugar compared with pure glucose. In the international tables from Sydney, table sugar scores about 65, and honey about 61.
sahneler.gorsel: a spoon of honey and a spoon of white sugar side by side on a wooden table, an antique stopwatch between them

sahneler.metin: That's close. And honeys vary a lot: individual honeys have been tested anywhere from about 32 to 87. So your own jar could land well above or below the average.
sahneler.gorsel: four different jars of honey in shades from pale to dark amber standing in a row, a honey dipper leaning on the nearest jar

sahneler.metin: Here's the catch with a lower score. Glycemic index doesn't tell you how much sugar is in the spoon. A tablespoon of honey weighs about 21 grams and holds roughly 64 calories and 17 grams of sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: a level tablespoon of honey on a kitchen scale, a jar of honey behind it, a small pile of sugar crystals beside it

sahneler.metin: That's why Mayo Clinic's diabetes experts say there's generally no advantage to swapping honey for sugar in a diabetes plan. Both raise blood sugar, and honey has slightly more carbohydrate per teaspoon.
sahneler.gorsel: a doctor's desk with a stethoscope, a glucose meter with a blank screen and a jar of honey with a spoon
sahneler.etiket: Mayo Clinic · Diabetes foods: honey for sugar

sahneler.metin: So why do headlines say honey might actually help? The answer starts in Toronto.
In 2022, a team led by Tauseef Khan and John Sievenpiper at the University of Toronto searched for controlled trials on honey and pooled the results.
sahneler.gorsel: a university library table with stacks of bound volumes, a jar of honey and an open notebook with blank pages, an antique lamp

sahneler.metin: That meant 18 trials, 33 comparisons, and 1,105 people. The typical trial lasted eight weeks and used about 40 grams of honey a day, roughly two tablespoons.
sahneler.gorsel: two tablespoons of honey side by side on a wooden board, a jar of honey behind them, a wall calendar with blank squares

sahneler.metin: Most trials compared honey with people's usual diet. Only seven comparisons used table sugar or high fructose corn syrup. In the practical part, I'll share a simple rule for how to count honey.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey beside a plate of ordinary breakfast foods, toast, an egg and a cup of tea, and a small bottle of corn syrup

sahneler.metin: Pooled together, honey lowered fasting glucose by about 4 milligrams per deciliter, total cholesterol by about 7, LDL cholesterol by about 6, and triglycerides by about 12.

grafik.kaynak: Ahmed et al., Nutr Rev 2022 · 18 trials, n = 1,105, median age 41 · converted from mmol/L

sahneler.metin: HDL, the so-called good cholesterol, rose by about 3 milligrams per deciliter, and that was the one result rated high certainty. Most of the others were rated low certainty.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with a small red heart symbol beside it, a honey dipper resting on a saucer

sahneler.metin: That's a modest change. The authors themselves noted that the cholesterol improvements look clinically trivial. So where did the big headlines come from?
sahneler.gorsel: a honey dipper lifting a thin thread of honey over a jar, a newspaper stack with blank pages in the background

sahneler.metin: The big numbers came from honey subgroups: raw honey, and honey from a single kind of flower.
Raw honey is honey that hasn't been processed. Single-flower honey comes mostly from one kind of blossom, such as clover, or robinia, which is also called acacia.
sahneler.gorsel: a raw honeycomb dripping into a glass jar of honey, a clover blossom and a branch of white robinia flowers beside it

sahneler.metin: In five trials of raw honey, fasting glucose fell by about 19 milligrams per deciliter. In two trials of clover honey, it fell by about 33.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of raw honey with a wooden honey dipper, a honeycomb, and a glucose meter with a blank screen

sahneler.metin: Here are those subgroup results next to the overall average. They look dramatic. But look at how few trials stand behind them.

grafik.baslik: Fasting glucose drop, by honey type
grafik.kaynak: Ahmed et al., Nutr Rev 2022 · 20, 5 and 2 comparisons, low certainty · converted from mmol/L

sahneler.metin: Five trials for raw honey. Two for clover. For robinia, the results come from a single trial, and they were for cholesterol, not glucose. The authors call these subgroup findings that need confirming.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with only a few small honeycomb pieces on a plate, a single clover flower in a tiny vase

sahneler.metin: They also say we need more research on floral source and processing. The Toronto team suggested that the heating used in commercial processing may reduce some of honey's benefits, but that is not settled.
sahneler.gorsel: a pot of warm water on a stove with a jar of honey standing beside it, a thermometer hanging on the pot, steam rising

sahneler.metin: One idea about why honey might behave differently is its fructose. In the glycemic tables, fructose scores just 15, while glucose scores 103. Honey has more fructose than glucose.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey beside a ripe pear and a few apple slices, a honeybee drawn above the honey

sahneler.metin: That's one reason honey scores a little below table sugar. But a little below is still a long way from a free pass.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey and a bowl of sugar crystals on the two pans of an old brass scale, the pans nearly level

sahneler.metin: Now, the honest part: why these results may be shakier than they look.
The authors checked for publication bias, the tendency for positive studies to get published more often. They found signs of it for fasting glucose.
sahneler.gorsel: a stack of journals with blank covers, a jar of honey sitting on top of the stack, an antique magnifying glass beside it

sahneler.metin: When they adjusted for that, the glucose drop shrank to about 2 milligrams per deciliter, and it was no longer statistically significant.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with a glucose meter with a blank screen, a dashed arrow curving gently downward and flattening out

sahneler.metin: Most trials also reported their methods poorly, and results differed a lot from one trial to the next. For LDL cholesterol, dropping any one of six particular trials made the effect disappear.
sahneler.gorsel: a tangled bundle of honey dippers of different lengths on a wooden table, a jar of honey in the background

sahneler.metin: Who took part matters too. The median age was about 41, only about one in five people had diabetes, and trials were short. That's very different from an older adult with years of type 2 diabetes.
sahneler.gorsel: a younger person's hands and an older person's hands on either side of a jar of honey on a kitchen table

sahneler.metin: A reminder from one trial in people with type 2 diabetes. In a randomized trial of 48 patients, eight weeks of natural honey, compared with no honey, was followed by a rise in HbA1c, the three-month blood sugar average.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with a spoon next to a laboratory sample tube in a rack, an antique notebook with blank pages
sahneler.etiket: Bahrami et al. · Int J Food Sci Nutr · 2009

sahneler.metin: A later commentary suggested that the high doses used may have played a part. It's one trial, but it shows that natural does not automatically mean safe for blood sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: a very large jar of honey with an overflowing spoon on a small saucer, a glucose meter with a blank screen nearby

sahneler.metin: An earlier trial of 55 overweight or obese adults gave 38 of them 70 grams of honey a day, and 17 the same amount of sucrose, for 30 days. In the honey group, weight and body fat slipped by about one percent.
sahneler.gorsel: two bowls on a table, one filled with honey and one with white sugar, each with a spoon, a measuring tape coiled beside them
sahneler.etiket: Yaghoobi et al. · Sci World J · 2008

sahneler.metin: It's small and short, so treat it as a hint, not proof. And honey is a lot of sugar to eat for a month.
sahneler.gorsel: a tall stack of honey jars on a pantry shelf, a small cloth over the top jar

sahneler.metin: There's also a note on funding. Several authors, including Khan and Sievenpiper, report research support from the National Honey Board. Most of the trials were publicly funded. It isn't a sign the work is wrong, just context.
sahneler.gorsel: a quiet office desk with a honey jar, a paper knife and a folded stack of paper with blank pages, a brass desk lamp

sahneler.metin: Also, these trials were in people eating healthy diets with added sugars at ten percent of calories or less. So the honey wasn't piled on top of lots of other sweets.
sahneler.gorsel: a balanced dinner plate with vegetables and fish and a small spoon of honey resting on its edge

sahneler.metin: Khan put it plainly: we are not saying you should start having honey if you currently avoid sugar. If anything, honey may help when it replaces another sweetener.
sahneler.gorsel: a spoon of honey replacing a spoon of sugar over a cup of tea, a curved dashed arrow between the two spoons

sahneler.metin: Now the math that headlines skip: calories, daily limits and what's on the jar.
Honey is about 80 percent sugar, and a tablespoon is roughly 64 calories. Two tablespoons, close to the amount in the typical trial, would be about 130 calories and 34 grams of sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: two level tablespoons of honey on a plate beside a jar of honey, a small pile of sugar crystals in the corner

sahneler.metin: The American Heart Association says most women should have no more than 100 calories a day from added sugars, about 25 grams or six teaspoons. For most men, it's 150 calories, about 36 grams or nine teaspoons.
sahneler.gorsel: a row of six level teaspoons of sugar on a wooden board beside a jar of honey, three more teaspoons stacked behind them

sahneler.metin: Sugars you add to food count, and that includes the honey you stir into tea or drizzle on toast. So two tablespoons of honey would be more than most women's daily limit, and almost all of most men's.
sahneler.gorsel: a cup of tea and a slice of toast with honey dripping from a dipper onto the toast, a jar of honey in the background

sahneler.metin: On the shelf, pure honey is a special case. The FDA does not require a grams line for added sugars on single-ingredient honey, but it does still require the percent daily value, so look for that on the jar.
sahneler.gorsel: a supermarket shelf with several honey jars of different sizes, a shopper's basket on the floor beside it

sahneler.metin: So how should you actually treat honey? Here are five practical points, and the rule I promised.
One. Treat honey as a sugar. If it replaces the sugar you'd use anyway, that's reasonable. If it goes on top of everything else, you're just adding sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: a cup of tea with a spoon of honey and an empty sugar bowl beside it, a jar of honey behind

sahneler.metin: Two. Count it. If you have diabetes, count honey's carbohydrate in your meal plan, just as you would sugar, which is what Mayo Clinic advises.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey with a spoon beside a meal plate with grilled fish and vegetables, a pencil resting on an open notebook with blank pages

sahneler.metin: Three. Measure it. A level teaspoon is a third of a tablespoon, so about 21 calories and 6 grams of sugar. A pour straight from the jar can easily be three times that.
sahneler.gorsel: a level teaspoon of honey on a kitchen scale, a drizzle of honey from a squeeze jar above it, a jar of honey nearby

sahneler.metin: Four. Choose honey for taste. If you like raw or single-flower honey, enjoy it. But the evidence doesn't yet show it works as a blood sugar tool, so don't pay extra for that reason.
sahneler.gorsel: a small wooden tasting board with three spoons of honey in pale, golden and dark amber shades, a jar of honey behind them

sahneler.metin: Five. A safety note. If you take diabetes medicine, especially insulin or pills that can cause low blood sugar, ask your doctor or pharmacist before changing how much sweetener you eat. And never give honey to a baby under one year old, because of infant botulism.
sahneler.gorsel: a pharmacy counter with a pill organizer, an insulin pen and a jar of honey with a spoon, a stethoscope on the side

sahneler.metin: If you use a home glucose meter, your own readings can show how your body responds to a spoonful. And if you've been told to watch your blood sugar, ask your care team whether any honey fits your plan.
sahneler.gorsel: a glucose meter with a blank screen beside a jar of honey and a small spoon, a phone lying face down

sahneler.metin: Let's recap.

kart.alt: A little better, not a free pass

sahneler.metin: Honey is mostly sugar. Its glycemic index of about 61 is only slightly below table sugar's 65, and a tablespoon still holds 64 calories and 17 grams of sugar.
sahneler.gorsel: a jar of honey beside a bowl of sugar on a kitchen table, a level tablespoon of honey on a saucer

sahneler.metin: A 2022 Toronto analysis of 18 trials found small average improvements, about 4 milligrams per deciliter in fasting glucose. But the evidence was mostly low certainty, and that glucose effect faded after adjusting for publication bias.
sahneler.gorsel: an open notebook with blank pages, a jar of honey and a glucose meter with a blank screen on a desk

sahneler.metin: Raw and single-flower honeys looked better, but those results rest on a handful of small trials, in people with a median age of 41. Whether they help older adults with diabetes is not known.
sahneler.gorsel: a raw honeycomb on a plate beside a jar of honey and a clover flower, an elderly pair of hands holding a spoon

sahneler.metin: So if honey replaces your sugar, enjoy it, measure it, and count it. Don't expect a miracle from the jar.
sahneler.gorsel: a cup of tea with a spoon of honey on a wooden table, a jar of honey with a dipper behind it, morning light

sahneler.metin: If you found this useful, subscribe to The Food Almanac for more food science, explained calmly and honestly. This video is for education only, and it isn't medical advice. See you in the next one.
